subject: humanities
passage: Ibn Khaldun, a scholar born in Tunis in 1332, served as an official at several North African courts before withdrawing from public life to write a history of the world. Completed in 1377 as the introduction to that history, ______ In it, he argued that a dynasty draws its strength from the loyalty that binds its founding group, a bond that tends to weaken over several generations.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the Muqaddimah examines why dynasties rise and fall.
choices.B: the question of why dynasties rise and fall is examined in the Muqaddimah.
choices.C: why dynasties rise and fall is examined by Ibn Khaldun in the Muqaddimah.
choices.D: Ibn Khaldun examined in the Muqaddimah why dynasties rise and fall.

explanation.why: The phrase "Completed in 1377 as the introduction to that history" describes a piece of writing, so the noun right after the comma must name that writing: the Muqaddimah. Ibn Khaldun himself was not "completed" as an introduction.
explanation.A: Correct. "The Muqaddimah" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear the book was completed in 1377.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This choice says "the question" was completed in 1377 as an introduction; the modifier must describe the book.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This choice says a question ("why dynasties rise and fall") was completed as the introduction, which makes no sense.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This choice places "Ibn Khaldun" after the phrase, saying the scholar himself was completed as an introduction.
